content.body:
## Overview The work-planner skill takes the file style its prosiform form will need, laying the groundwork for prosiform compliance before the skill's extraction is cut. The style is the one the example skill under `.project/main/example` shows. That example is an older work-planner and serves as a structural style reference only: no content carries over from it. Command presentation follows the linked Graph Index example in R5. Context is selected through in-text links, and no prosiform metadata is added. ## Problem - **Steps are list items.** Every procedure is a numbered list with bold leads, so a step has no heading to link and no place for its own detail. - **Command contracts are implicit.** Invocations lack contextual input and output links, while usage details and repeated parameter inventories obscure their execution contract. - **Inputs and outputs lack explicit roles.** Command specifications do not consistently link every consumed or provided value to its owning Field, leaving part of the execution contract implied. - **SKILL.md carries the rules.** The rules and conventions that bind every mode, and the deployment values, sit in SKILL.md and the guidelines rather than in files of their own. - **The style model describes the installed layout.** The current declarations and checks do not define the proposed heading-based steps, linked contracts and HTML command blocks. ## Proposal - **Per-skill style model.** The skill's own guidelines, `structure.json` and `rules.json` state the new model, and the shared checker reads each skill's declared model. - The shared guidelines and every other skill keep their current shape. - Checker support is proven against specimen skills before document conversion. The final task adopts Work Planner's new guidelines and model declarations once every conversion is complete; the installed declarations govern the live checks until that adoption. - **Entry files.** SKILL.md keeps its opening, Modes and Dependencies. - `rules.md` holds the rules that bind every mode, `conventions.md` the conventions, and `configuration.md` the deployment values, each built from the live skill's own text. - **Steps as sub-sections.** Each step is a heading of its position and action. A step with multiple contained instruction or detail items bullets every item; a single item is plain text. - Calls use Run for a command, Apply for an artifact operation and Follow for a mode, protocol or child procedure. - Each mode and protocol opens with the preamble line that links Rules, Conventions and, for a mode, Outcomes. - **Named command specifications.** A `## Commands` section precedes Fields and holds each enriched invocation once. Its imperative preamble states the action and provides its linked output to the requester. Operations call commands with the necessary selections, conditions and continuations. Linked arguments establish their contracts without a repeated parameter list in prose. - Value-format and output examples appear on the owning Field's description line as `eg` with inline code. Structural templates keep their fences. Single-sentence conditions accompany the command preamble; multi-item command details follow the invocation. - Command and tool-access invocations use raw HTML `
…
` blocks, matching the specific R5 step. Contract-backed input names are bold Markdown links inside the block, using role-tagged `[**argument**](#argument-contract "○")`. Long shell invocations use backslash-newline continuations at token boundaries, grouping options with their values while preserving literal syntax and argument order. Shell quoting follows the value type: validated shell-safe numbers/identifiers and fixed safe literals are unquoted; variable paths, refs, free text and query expressions retain their required quoting. - Checker fixtures accept this HTML command form and its resolving argument links, and reject Markdown-fenced command invocations. The example supplies presentation only; its tool names, graph behavior, content and metadata are outside this migration. - **Inputs, outputs and contracts.** Each command links every consumed input and provided output to its owning `###` Field in contextual prose or the invocation. Nested operations do not repeat I/O contracts. Markdown link titles mark `"○"` for input, `"●"` for output and `"ƒ"` for a called command, operation, protocol or procedure. Results use Provide. `rules.md` defines the tags, and the guidelines require an independent completeness check against commands, calls, conditions and results. Performed-operation contract verification remains a future feature. - Fields define scalar or composite data objects and valid-state constraints. A single-use rule belongs with its caller; shared policy has one linked Guidance home. Artifact operations own shared procedures with meaningful decisions or processing. - In-text links select context at its use. The skill has no Prerequisites inventories. - **Scope.** The migration preserves operational behavior and frontmatter. - No prosiform metadata, no `pf` instruction and no prosiform link marks, which need its grammar to place. - No file or rule is taken from the example's content. ## Work Breakdown | Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1640) | Per-skill style model and checker | AC1 | | | | ✓ | | [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1642) | Rules, conventions and configuration files | AC2 | W01 | | | ✓ | | [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1643) | Modes in the new style | AC3 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1644) | Protocols in the new style | AC4 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W05](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1646) | Issue and body artifacts in the new style | AC5 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W06](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1651) | Board, queue, planning and review artifacts restyled | AC6 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W07](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1647) | Delivery, branch and pull-request artifacts restyled | AC7 | W02 | | | ✓ | | [W08](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1652) | Activate the Work Planner style model | AC8 | W03, W04, W05, W06, W07 | | | ✓ | ## Acceptance Criteria - [x] **AC1.** `check_skill_files.py` validates specimen declarations of the proposed Work Planner style model, including its command style, as acceptance/rejection fixtures show. - [x] **AC2.** SKILL.md holds only its opening, Modes and Dependencies, and `rules.md`, `conventions.md` and `configuration.md` hold what binds every mode, checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC3.** Every mode states its steps as sub-sections, opens with the preamble line and calls through Run, Apply and Follow, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC4.** Every protocol states its steps as sub-sections, opens with the preamble line and calls through Run, Apply and Follow, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC5.** Every issue and body artifact holds enriched invocation specifications in Commands before Fields and links every command input and output at its actual use with its role title, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC6.** Every board, queue, planning and review artifact holds enriched invocation specifications in Commands before Fields and links every command input and output at its actual use with its role title, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC7.** Every delivery, branch and pull-request artifact holds enriched invocation specifications in Commands before Fields and links every command input and output at its actual use with its role title, using the [command style](#proposal), checked by Check Skill Files. - [x] **AC8.** The Work Planner guidelines, `structure.json` and `rules.json` declare the new style model over the converted skill, with zero findings from Check Skill Files over `skills/work-planner`. ## References - **R1.** [Planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-11-02-1597-i17-pre-cutover-fixes) — the decisions, the artifact grouping and each task's work item. - **R2.** [Example skill](https://github.com/m2ux/md-composer/tree/00f166920ec242f3565376e06a8838de72f8dc34/example/work-planner) — the older work-planner whose file style this epic adopts; style only. - **R3.** [Example guidelines](https://github.com/m2ux/md-composer/blob/00f166920ec242f3565376e06a8838de72f8dc34/example/guidelines.md) — the shared guidelines that state that style. - **R4.** [Work Planner at the migration baseline](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/03d353300ca4804194fd50d316d73e3bf1270d1d/skills/work-planner) — the skill this epic restyles. - **R5.** [HTML command-style example](https://github.com/shieldedtech/midnight-agent-eng/blob/a710a42e82df7f18b27f8a6cfa4b6e9c801df903/skills/finding-classifier/artifacts/graph-index.md#1-fetch-the-first-inventory-page) — the specific command presentation adopted by this migration; style only.
